paper.title: Is the Scientific Paper a Fraud?

blocks.en: I HAVE chosen for my title a question: Is the scientific paper a fraud? I ought to explain that a scientific "paper" is a printed communication to a learned journal, and scientists make their work known almost wholly through papers and not through books, so papers are very important in scientific communication. As to what I mean by asking "is the scientific paper a fraud?" —I do not, of course, mean "Does the scientific paper misrepresent facts?" and I do not mean that the interpretations you find in a scientific paper are wrong or deliberately mistaken. I mean the scientific paper may be a fraud because it misrepresents the processes of thought that accompanied or gave rise to the work that is described in the paper.
blocks.zh: 我选了一个问题作为题目：科学论文是骗局吗？先说明一下，所谓科学‘论文’，就是刊登在学术期刊上的书面报告。科学家几乎完全通过论文，而不是书籍，来公布自己的工作，因此论文在科学交流中极为重要。至于我问‘科学论文是骗局吗？’，当然不是在问论文是否歪曲事实，也不是说论文中的解释有误，或是作者故意作出错误解释。我的意思是，科学论文之所以可能是一种骗局，在于它歪曲了伴随、或促成论文所述工作的那些思维过程。
blocks.translation_method: human-translated spot correction

blocks.en: That is the question, and I will say right away that my answer to it is "yes." The scientific paper in its orthodox form does embody a totally mistaken conception, even a travesty, of the nature of scientific thought.
blocks.zh: 这就是问题所在，我会立即说我的答案是“是”。正统形式的科学论文确实体现了对科学思想本质的完全错误的概念，甚至是嘲讽。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Just consider for a moment the traditional form of a scientific paper (incidentally, it is a form which editors themselves often insist upon). The structure of a scientific paper in the biological sciences is something like this: First, there is a section called the "introduction" in which you merely describe the general field in which your scientific talents are going to be exercised, followed by a section called "previous work" in which you concede, more or less graciously, that others have dimly groped toward the fundamental truths that you are now about to expound. Then a section on "methods"— that is O.K. Then comes the section called "results."
blocks.zh: 考虑一下科学论文的传统形式（顺便说一句，这是编辑自己经常坚持的形式）。生物科学中的科学论文的结构是这样的：首先，有一个称为“引言”的部分，在其中您仅描述将要发挥您的科学才能的一般领域，然后是一个称为“先前工作”的部分，在其中您或多或少亲切地承认，其他人已经模糊地摸索了您现在要阐述的基本真理。然后是关于“方法”的部分——没关系。然后是“结果”部分。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: The section called "results" consists of a stream of factual information in which it is considered extremely bad form to discuss the significance of the results you are getting. You have to pretend that your mind is, so to speak, a virgin receptacle, an empty vessel, for information which floods into it from the external world for no reason which you yourself have revealed. You reserve all appraisal of the scientific evidence until the "discussion" section, and in the discussion you adopt the ludicrous pretense of asking yourself if the information you have collected actually means anything.
blocks.zh: 称为“结果”的部分由一系列事实信息组成，在其中讨论您所获得的结果的重要性被认为是极其糟糕的形式。可以说，你必须假装你的思想是一个处女容器，一个空容器，用于容纳从外部世界涌入的信息，而你自己也没有透露任何原因。你保留对科学证据的所有评估，直到“讨论”部分，并且在讨论中你采取可笑的假装问自己所收集的信息是否实际上意味着什么。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Of course, what I am saying is rather an exaggeration, but there is more than a mere element of truth in it.
blocks.zh: 当然，我说的有些夸张，但其中不乏真实的成分。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: The conception underlying this style of scientific writing is that scientific discovery is an inductive process. What induction implies in its cruder form is roughly speaking this: Scientific discovery,, or the formulation of scientific theory, starts in with the unvarnished and unembroidered evidence of the senses. It starts with simple observation —simple, unbiased, unprejudiced, naive, or innocent observation—and out of this sensory evidence, embodied in the form of simple propositions or declarations of fact, generalizations will grow up and take shape, almost as if some process of crystalization or condensation were taking place. Out of a disorderly array of facts, an orderly theory, an orderly general statement, will somehow emerge.
blocks.zh: 这种科学写作风格的基本概念是科学发现是一个归纳过程。归纳法的粗略含义大致是这样的：科学发现，或者科学理论的表述，始于感官的朴实无华的证据。它从简单的观察开始——简单的、公正的、不带偏见的、天真的或无害的观察——并且从这种以简单命题或事实声明的形式体现的感官证据中，概括将会成长并形成，几乎就像正在发生某种结晶或凝结的过程一样。从一堆无序的事实中，会以某种方式出现有序的理论、有序的一般性陈述。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: THIS conception of scientific discovery was mainly the work of a great and wise, but in this context. I think, very mistaken man—John Stuart Mill.
blocks.zh: 这种科学发现的概念主要是伟大而智者的作品，但在这种背景下。我想，约翰·斯图尔特·密尔，这是一个非常错误的人。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: John Stuart Mill saw, as of course a great many others, including Bacon, had seen before him that deduction in itself is quite powerless as a method of scientific discover)--and for this simple reason: that the process of deduction as such only uncovers, brings out into the open, makes explicit, information that is already present in the axioms or premises from which the process of deduction started. The process of deduction reveals nothing to us except what the infirmity of our own minds has so far concealed from us.
blocks.zh: 约翰·斯图尔特·密尔（John Stuart Mill）认为，就像包括培根在内的许多其他人在他之前看到的那样，演绎本身作为一种科学发现的方法是相当无能为力的）——原因很简单：演绎过程本身只能揭示、公开、明确已经存在于演绎过程开始的公理或前提中的信息。演绎过程除了向我们揭示我们自己思想的弱点迄今为止所隐藏的东西之外，什么也没有向我们揭示。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: It was Mill's belief that induction was the method of science—"that great mental operation," he called it, "the operation of discovering and proving general propositions." And around this conception there grew up an inductive logic, of which the business was "to provide rules to which, if inductive arguments conform, those arguments are conclusive."
blocks.zh: 密尔相信归纳法是科学的方法——他称之为“伟大的心理运作”，“发现和证明一般命题的运作”。围绕这一概念，出现了一种归纳逻辑，其任务是“提供规则，如果归纳论证符合这些规则，那么这些论证就是结论性的”。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Now, John Stuart Mill's deeper motive in working out what he conceived to be the essential method of science was to apply that method to the solution of sociological problems: He wanted to apply to sociology the methods which the practice of science had shown to be immensely powerful and exact. It is ironical that the application to sociology of the inductive method, more or less in the form in which Mill himself conceived it, should have been an almost entirely fruitless one.
blocks.zh: 现在，约翰·斯图尔特·密尔制定他所认为的科学基本方法的更深层动机是将这种方法应用于社会学问题的解决：他想将科学实践已证明非常强大和精确的方法应用于社会学。具有讽刺意味的是，归纳法在社会学中的应用，或多或少以密尔本人设想的形式，几乎是完全没有结果的。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: The simplest application of the Millsian process of induction to sociology came in a rather strange movement called Mass Observation. The belief underlying Mass Observation was apparently this: that if one could only record and set down the actual raw facts about what people do and what people say in pubs, in trains, when they make love to each other, when they are playing games, and so on, then somehow, from this wealth of information, a great generalization would inevitably emerge.
blocks.zh: 米尔斯归纳法在社会学中最简单的应用是一场相当奇怪的运动，称为大众观察。大众观察背后的信念显然是这样的：如果人们只能记录和记录人们在酒吧、火车上、当他们做爱时、当他们玩游戏时等等的行为和言论的真实原始事实，那么不知何故，从这些丰富的信息中，不可避免地会出现一种伟大的概括。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Well, in point of fact, nothing important emerged from this approach.
blocks.zh: 嗯，事实上，这种方法并没有产生任何重要的结果。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: THE theory underlying the inductive method cannot be sustained. Let me give three good reasons why not.
blocks.zh: 归纳法的理论不能成立。让我给出三个不这样做的充分理由。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: In the first place, the starting point of induction is philosophic fiction. There is no such thing as unprejudiced observation. Every act of observation we make is biased. What we see or otherwise sense is a function of what we have seen or sensed in the past.
blocks.zh: 首先，归纳的起点是哲学小说。不存在不带偏见的观察。我们所做的每一个观察行为都是有偏见的。我们所看到或感觉到的东西是我们过去所看到或感觉到的东西的函数。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: The second point is this: Scientific discovery or the formulation of the scientific idea on the one hand, and demonstration or proof on the other hand, are two entirely different notions. Mill confused them. Mill said that induction was the "operation of discovering and proving general propositions," as if one act of mind would do for both.
blocks.zh: 第二点是：一方面是科学发现或科学思想的表述，另一方面是论证或证明，是两个完全不同的概念。米尔让他们感到困惑。密尔说，归纳法是“发现和证明一般命题的操作”，就好像一种思维行为可以同时实现两者一样。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Now, discovery and proof could depend on the same act of mind, and in deduction they do. When we indulge in the process of deduction—as in deducing a theorem from Euclidian axioms or postulates—the theorem contains the discovery (or, more exactly, the uncovery of something which was there in the axioms and postulates, though it was not actually evident) and the process of deduction itself, if it has been carried out correctly, is also the proof that the "discovery" is valid, is logically correct. So in the process of deduction, discovery and proof can depend on the same process. But in scientific activity they are not the same thing—they are, in fact, totally separate acts of mind.
blocks.zh: 现在，发现和证明可能依赖于相同的思维行为，在演绎中它们也是如此。当我们沉迷于演绎过程时——就像从欧几里得公理或公设中演绎出一个定理——该定理包含了发现（或者更准确地说，揭示了公理和公设中存在的某些东西，尽管它实际上并不明显），而演绎过程本身，如果执行得正确，也证明了“发现”是有效的，在逻辑上是正确的。所以在演绎的过程中，发现和证明可以依赖于同一个过程。但在科学活动中，它们不是同一件事——事实上，它们是完全不同的思维行为。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: It simply is not logically possible to arrive with certainty at any generalization containing more information than the sum of the particular statements upon which the generalization was founded. How could a mere act of mind lead to the discovery of new information? It would violate a law as fundamental as the law of conservation of matter. It would violate the law of conservation of information.
blocks.zh: 从逻辑上讲，不可能肯定地得出任何包含比该概括所依据的特定陈述的总和更多信息的概括。单纯的思想行为怎么可能导致新信息的发现呢？它将违反物质守恒定律这样的基本法则。这将违反信息守恒定律。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: In view of all these objections, it is hardly surprising that Bertrand Russell in a famous footnote that occurs in his Principles of Mathematics of 1903 should have said that, so far as he could see, induction was a method of making plausible guesses. And our greatest modern authority on the nature of scientific method. Professor Karl Popper, has no use for induction at all: He regards the inductive process of thought as a myth. "There is no need even to mention induction," he says in his great treatise, on The Logic of Scientific Discovery—though, of course, he does mention it.
blocks.zh: 鉴于所有这些反对意见，伯特兰·罗素 (Bertrand Russell) 在其 1903 年《数学原理》中的著名脚注中表示，就他而言，归纳法是一种做出合理猜测的方法，这一点也就不足为奇了。也是我们关于科学方法本质的最伟大的现代权威。卡尔·波普尔教授根本没有使用归纳法：他认为归纳思维过程是一个神话。 “甚至没有必要提及归纳法，”他在关于科学发现的逻辑的伟大论文中说道，尽管他当然提到了这一点。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: NOW let me go back to the scientific papers. What is wrong with the traditional form of scientific paper is simply this: that all scientific work of an experimental or exploratory character starts with some expectation about the outcome of the inquiry. This expectation one starts with, this hypothesis one formulates, provides the initiative and incentive for the inquiry and governs its actual form. It is in the light of this expectation that some observations are held relevant and others not; that some methods are chosen, others discarded; that some experiments are done rather than others. It is only in the light of this prior expectation that the activities the scientist reports in his scientific papers really have any meaning at all.
blocks.zh: 现在让我回到科学论文。科学论文的传统形式的问题很简单：所有具有实验性或探索性的科学工作都是从对调查结果的某种期望开始的。人们从这一期望出发，提出这一假设，为探究提供了主动性和激励，并决定了其实际形式。正是鉴于这种期望，一些观察结果具有相关性，而另一些则不相关；选择了一些方法，放弃了另一些方法；进行一些实验而不是其他实验。只有考虑到这种预先的期望，科学家在其科学论文中报告的活动才真正有意义。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: Hypotheses arise by guesswork. That is to put it in its crudest form. I should say rather that they arise by inspiration; but in any event they arise by processes that form part of the subjectmatter of psychology and certainly not of logic, for there is no logically rigorous method for devising hypotheses. It is a vulgar error, often committed, to speak of "deducing" hypotheses. Indeed one does not deduce hypotheses; hypotheses are what one deduces things from.
blocks.zh: 假设是由猜测产生的。也就是说，以最原始的形式表达它。我应该说它们是由灵感产生的。但无论如何，它们是由构成心理学主题一部分的过程产生的，当然不是逻辑主题的一部分，因为没有逻辑上严格的方法来设计假设。谈论“演绎”假设是一个经常犯的粗俗错误。事实上，人们并不推导出假设；而是推论出假设。假设是人们从中推断出事物的东西。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: But hypotheses can be tested rigorously—they are tested by experiment, using the word "experiment" in a rather general sense to mean an act performed to test a hypothesis, that is, to test the deductive consequences of a hypothesis. If one formulates a hypothesis, one can deduce from it certain consequences which are predictions or declarations about what will or will not be the case. If these predictions and declarations are mistaken, then the hypothesis must be discarded, or at least modified. If, on the other hand, the predictions turn out correct, then the hypothesis has stood up to trial, and remains on probation as before.
blocks.zh: 但假设可以经过严格检验——它们是通过实验来检验的，“实验”一词在相当普遍的意义上是指为检验假设而进行的行为，即检验假设的演绎结果。如果一个人提出一个假设，就可以从中推断出某些后果，这些后果是关于情况会发生或不会发生的预测或声明。如果这些预测和声明是错误的，那么这个假设就必须被放弃，或者至少被修改。另一方面，如果预测结果是正确的，那么该假设就经受住了考验，并且像以前一样处于试用状态。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: This formulation illustrates very well, I think, the distinction between, on the one hand, the discovery or formulation of a scientific idea or generalization, which is to a greater or lesser degree an imaginative or inspirational act, and, on the other hand, the proof, or rather the testing of a hypothesis, which is indeed a strictly logical and rigorous process, based upon deductive arguments. T THIS alternative interpretation of the nature of the scientific process, of the nature of scientific method, is sometimes called the hypothetico-deductive interpretation. And this is the view which Professor Karl Popper has persuaded us is the correct one.
blocks.zh: 我认为，这个表述很好地说明了两者之间的区别：一方面，科学思想或概括的发现或表述，或多或少是一种想象力或灵感的行为；另一方面，证明，或者更确切地说是对假设的检验，这确实是一个基于演绎论证的严格逻辑和严谨的过程。这种对科学过程的本质、科学方法的本质的另一种解释有时被称为假说—演绎解释。卡尔·波普尔教授让我们相信这一观点是正确的。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: To give credit where credit is surely due, it is proper to say that the first professional scientist to express a fully reasoned opinion upon the way scientists actually think when they come upon their scientific discoveries—namely William Whewell, a geologist, and incidentally the Master of Trinity College, Cambridge—was also the first person to formulate this hypothetico-deductive interpretation of scientific activity. Whewell, like his contemporary Mill, wrote at great length—unnecessarily great length, one is nowadays inclined to think—and I cannot recapitulate his argument, but one or two quotations will make the gist of his thought clear. He said: "An art of discovery is not possible. We can give no rules for the pursuit of truth which should be universally and peremptorily applicable." And of hypotheses he said, with great daring, "a facility in devising hypotheses, so far from being a fault in the intellectual character of a discoverer, is a faculty indispensable to his task."
blocks.zh: 为了给予肯定应有的赞扬，可以正确地说，第一个对科学家在获得科学发现时的实际思考方式表达了充分合理的意见的专业科学家——即地质学家威廉·惠厄尔，顺便说一句，剑桥三一学院的院长——也是第一个对科学活动提出这种假说—演绎解释的人。休厄尔和他同时代的密尔一样，写了很长的文章——现在人们倾向于思考不必要的长篇大论——我无法概括他的论点，但一两段引文将使他的思想要点变得清晰。他说：“发现的艺术是不可能的。我们不能为追求真理制定任何规则，而这些规则应该是普遍和绝对适用的。”在谈到假设时，他非常大胆地说，“提出假设的能力绝不是发现者智力上的缺陷，而是他的任务中不可或缺的能力。”
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked

blocks.en: I said this was daring because the word "hypothesis" and the conception it stood for was still in Whewell's day a rather discreditable one. Hypotheses had a flavor about them of what was wanton and irresponsible. The great Newton, you remember, had frowned upon hypotheses. "Hypotheses non fingo," he said, and there is another version in which he says "hypotheses non sequor"—I do not pursue hypotheses.
blocks.zh: 我说这番话大胆，是因为在休厄尔的时代，‘假说’这个词及其所代表的观念，仍颇有些声名不佳。假说让人联想到任意妄为和不负责任。你们记得，伟大的牛顿就曾对假说皱眉。他说过‘Hypotheses non fingo’；还有一种说法是‘hypotheses non sequor’——我不追随假说。
blocks.translation_method: human-translated spot correction

blocks.en: So to go back once again to the scientific paper: The scientific paper is a fraud in the sense that it does give a totally misleading narrative of the processes of thought that go into the making of scientific discoveries. The inductive format of the scientific paper should be discarded. The discussion which in the traditional scientific paper goes last should surely come at the beginning. The scientific facts and scientific acts should follow the discussion, and scientists should not be ashamed to admit, as many of them apparently are ashamed to admit, that hypotheses appear in their minds along uncharted by-ways of thought; that they are imaginative and inspirational in character; that they are indeed adventures of the mind.
blocks.zh: 因此，再次回到科学论文：科学论文是一种欺诈，因为它确实对科学发现的思维过程进行了完全误导性的叙述。科学论文的归纳格式应该被抛弃。传统科学论文中最后进行的讨论当然应该出现在开头。科学事实和科学行为应该遵循讨论，科学家不应该羞于承认，就像他们中的许多人显然羞于承认的那样，假设沿着未知的思维方式出现在他们的头脑中；他们的性格富有想象力和鼓舞人心；它们确实是心灵的冒险。
blocks.translation_method: machine-draft; source order and terminology checked
